title: Drive a SIL board emulator from Java
skills_assessed: TCP client to a SIL emulator
before_you_start: OpenJDK 21, Maven, the SIL board emulator, and the stubbed Java controller are on the desktop.

role.title: Embedded / Java systems engineer
role.company_context: Engineering consultancy placing people on aerospace, defence, railway, and energy programs. Hardware often sits in the lab; day-to-day Java work is SIL controllers, protocol debug, and Linux-class device software rather than Spring microservices or bare-metal C. Hiring to strengthen Java engineers who can close the loop against a board emulator.
day_to_day: Write and review Java that talks framed protocols to boards, benches, and SIL emulators
Parse checksummed telemetry and apply threshold or interlock command logic
Keep health and status endpoints predictable so a reviewer or test bench can curl the controller
Pair with C/C++ and systems engineers on “works against the emulator → works on the bench” issues
Improve shared Maven templates and SIL harness conventions
required_skills: Comfortable building Java 21 with Maven (compile, exec:java)
Can implement a TCP client that reads and writes line-oriented frames
Can validate a checksum and ignore malformed or corrupt frames
Can apply a documented threshold and send a command, then prove it with HTTP and emulator output
nice_to_have_skills: Familiarity with com.sun.net.httpserver or similar JDK HTTP APIs
Experience with SIL/MIL harnesses or serial/Ethernet protocol debug
Experience with the VS Code Java Extension Pack
Comfort reading Maven compiler output when a process fails to start
constraints: Assessment focuses on completing the provided Maven controller against the provided SIL emulator — not redesigning the stack, adding Spring, or flashing real hardware
Do not test QEMU, MicroEJ, GPIO libraries, Kubernetes, or cloud IaC in this challenge
Candidate works in a desktop environment with Terminal, JDK 21, and Maven available
Starter files on the desktop are shared scenery; do not require inventing a different protocol or emulator

problem_statement.title: Close the loop on the SIL emulator
problem_statement.summary: A SIL board emulator and a stubbed Maven Java controller are on your desktop. The HTTP server already compiles and listens. Implement the TCP client and handlers so the controller parses checksummed SENS frames, commands the actuator when the sensor crosses the threshold, and serves GET /, GET /health, and GET /status.
outcomes: Build the Maven project. Start the emulator, then the controller, so HTTP is served on the documented default port.
GET / and GET /health return HTTP 200 with the documented JSON payloads.
The controller sends a valid CMD ON after a valid trip SENS. GET /status reflects the last good reading and command. The emulator prints SCENARIO PASS.
constraints: Do not change the public paths: GET /, GET /health, and GET /status must be the routes a reviewer curls.
Keep com.sun.net.httpserver and the Maven project; do not replace them with Spring or extra Maven dependencies.

Do not modify BoardEmulator.java. Use the documented ASCII SENS/CMD frames and XOR checksum (Protocol helpers). Drop malformed lines and bad checksums; trip only when value is strictly greater than the threshold.
The process should listen on a port you can curl (default HTTP port is 3000 unless you document otherwise). Prefer 0.0.0.0 as in the starter. Emulator TCP port is 9100 (or EMU_PORT).
Starter files on the desktop stay as shared scenery — treat them as the application source you complete; do not change the emulator sequence.
problem_statement.deliverables: Leave a Maven project a reviewer can rebuild and run from this desktop without guessing. Start the emulator, then the controller. Demonstrate GET /health and GET /status with curl or a browser, and the emulator stdout line SCENARIO PASS.

rubric.name: Working loop
rubric.summary: Demonstrates emulator plus app running, GET /health HTTP 200, and emulator SCENARIO PASS.
rubric.description: YES/NO: Did the candidate demonstrate the emulator and controller running, a successful GET /health with HTTP 200 through the instance’s documented default HTTP port (see starter Main.java / brief), AND emulator stdout SCENARIO PASS? Answer YES only if video or narrative shows both the health check and SCENARIO PASS. Compile-only, health-only, crash-on-start, or inferred “probably works” = NO. YES = full points; NO or unclear = 0.

rubric.name: Correct command
rubric.summary: Sends CMD actuator ON after a valid SENS above threshold; GET /status matches.
rubric.description: YES/NO: Does the leftover client send CMD,<actuator_id>,ON,<checksum> only after a valid SENS whose numeric value is strictly greater than the instance threshold, and does GET /status report that sensor id, a value above threshold, and command ON? Answer YES only if both the leftover client logic and /status match the instance sensor/actuator/threshold (see DeviceClient constants / scenario.md / brief). Hardcoded PASS without speaking the protocol, wrong actuator, command on nominal-only frames, or /status that does not show the trip = NO. YES = full points; NO or unclear = 0.

rubric.name: Protocol hygiene
rubric.summary: Uses ASCII SENS/CMD frames and the XOR checksum; drops bad frames.
rubric.description: YES/NO: Does the leftover client use the documented ASCII frames and XOR checksum (via Protocol helpers or equivalent), and are malformed / bad-checksum lines not treated as trips? Answer YES only if checksum validation is visible in the client path. Raw guess-the-command on a timer, a rewritten BoardEmulator, or treating the emulator’s bad-checksum high-value frame as a trip = NO. YES = full points; NO or unclear = 0.

rubric.name: Clarity of deliverables
rubric.summary: Leaves a rebuildable Maven project a reviewer can compile and run without guessing steps.
rubric.description: YES/NO: Is there a pom.xml plus sources left on the desktop that a reviewer could mvn-compile, then run the emulator (com.example.emu.BoardEmulator) and the controller (com.example.app.Main) without guessing paths or undocumented steps? Answer YES if the primary build artifact is present and self-explanatory enough to rebuild; optional notes must be accurate if present. No Maven project / cannot rebuild from the workspace = NO. YES = full points; NO or unclear = 0.

invariants: Keep the same skills_assessed and rubric structure/weights
Keep the same deliverable kinds and difficulty band (Maven Java SIL controller + provided TCP emulator)
Keep ASCII SENS/CMD frames, XOR checksum, JDK HttpServer, GET /, GET /health, GET /status, and trip-on-strictly-greater-than
Do not introduce Spring, extra Maven dependencies, QEMU, MicroEJ, GPIO libraries, Docker, or Kubernetes
Do not put a solved DeviceClient or Handlers under workspace/; do not rewrite Protocol checksum math

apply.candidate_brief:
## Drive the {{service_label}}

Hardware for {{device_context}} is at the lab. A SIL board emulator is on your desktop. The HTTP server already compiles, binds, and registers GET /, GET /health, and GET /status. The handlers return HTTP 501 and the TCP client is stubbed. Implement the controller so it talks the documented ASCII protocol, commands the actuator when the sensor crosses the threshold, and serves the documented JSON.

### Outcomes
- Build the Maven project. Start the emulator, then the controller, so the controller listens on the documented HTTP port.
- Serve GET / and GET /health with HTTP 200 and the documented JSON payloads.
- Connect to the emulator, parse checksummed SENS frames, and send `CMD,{{actuator_id}},ON,<checksum>` when `{{sensor_id}}` is strictly greater than `{{threshold}}`. Prove it with GET /status and the emulator's `SCENARIO PASS` line.

### Constraints
- Keep the public paths GET /, GET /health, and GET /status. Do not replace `com.sun.net.httpserver` or the Maven project with a different stack (no Spring and no extra Maven dependencies).
- Do not modify `BoardEmulator.java`. Treat it as the board. Use `Protocol` helpers for framing and the XOR checksum; drop malformed lines and bad checksums.
- Listen on a port a reviewer can curl (default HTTP port is {{default_port}} unless you document otherwise). Prefer HOST 0.0.0.0 as in the starter. Emulator TCP port is {{emu_port}} (or `EMU_PORT`).
- Starter files on the desktop stay as shared scenery — treat them as the application source you complete; do not change the emulator sequence.

### Deliverables
Leave a Maven project a reviewer can rebuild (`mvn -q compile`) and run without guessing: emulator via `mvn -q compile exec:java -Dexec.mainClass=com.example.emu.BoardEmulator`, controller via `mvn -q exec:java`. Demonstrate GET /health and GET /status with curl or a browser, and the emulator stdout line `SCENARIO PASS`.
